project.name: dbt Semantic Designer
project.description: A VS Code extension that visualises semantic (FK-based) relationships between dbt models within curated business domains, and enables interactive design of new models, columns, and relationships before they are built. Built items appear in green; planned items appear in orange. The dbt repo becomes the single source of truth for both lineage and semantic relationships.

tech_stack.runtime: VS Code Extension (Node.js host + browser webview)

phases.name: Foundation — Extension Scaffold + Read-Only Viewer
phases.description: Get a working VS Code extension that displays semantic domain graphs in read-only mode. Open VS Code in a dbt project, see semantic domains in the sidebar, click a domain to open a graph editor showing models and FK edges with colour-coded status.

phases.name: Interactive Design — Create Models, Columns, and Relationships
phases.description: Enable interactive design of new models and relationships using a single-mode approach. No browse/design toggle — the visual distinction between built (green) and planned (orange) items IS the mode indicator. Click any model to select it; the detail panel shows edit controls for planned items. Add new design models (orange), define columns, draw FK relationships, and persist all changes to the semantic domain JSON file.

phases.name: Domain Management + Auto-Reconciliation
phases.description: Full CRUD on domains and automatic orange-to-green transitions. Create and delete domains, add existing manifest models to domains, file watchers detect manifest changes, and design models automatically transition when they appear in the compiled manifest.

phases.name: Polish + Developer Experience
phases.description: Quality of life improvements, performance optimizations, and edge case handling. Keyboard shortcuts, context menus, search, minimap, export, and error handling.

phases.name: AI-Driven Modelling Metadata
phases.description: Enrich the semantic JSON schema with structured modelling metadata that AI populates during design. Grain statements, model roles, SCD strategies, and additive types become first-class fields that the extension renders, validates, and enforces. Expanded AI reasoning fields explain the rationale behind each structural decision, making AI-assisted modelling transparent and auditable.

features.name: Set up extension project scaffold
features.description: Create the VS Code extension project structure with esbuild dual build (extension host + webview), two TypeScript configs (tsconfig.json for Node.js and tsconfig.webview.json for DOM), package.json with extension manifest contribution points (commands, views, custom editor, settings, activation events), and .vscodeignore. Include the full directory structure as specified in the plan: src/ (extension host), webview/ (React), media/, test/.
validation_criteria: Run 'npm run build' and verify both extension host and webview bundles are produced without errors
Run 'tsc --noEmit' for both tsconfigs and verify no type errors
Open project in VS Code and press F5 — Extension Development Host window launches
Verify package.json contains all contribution points: commands, viewsContainers, views, customEditors, configuration, activationEvents
features.implementation_notes: esbuild.js handles dual build targets. Extension host targets Node.js, webview targets browser/DOM. Use 'workspaceContains:**/dbt_project.yml' as activation event. Custom editor selector: '**/models/semantic/**/*.json' with priority 'option'.

features.name: Implement ManifestService with streaming JSON parser
features.description: Create ManifestService (src/services/manifestService.ts) that stream-parses the ~43MB target/manifest.json using stream-json. Only extract the 'nodes' section — skip macros, sources, exposures, metrics to minimise memory. Provide methods: loadManifest(projectPath), getModelColumns(modelName), hasModel(modelName), getModelNames(), and invalidate(). Cache parsed model data in memory.
validation_criteria: Unit test: loadManifest parses a sample manifest fixture and returns model data
Unit test: getModelColumns returns correct columns for a known model
Unit test: hasModel returns true for existing models, false for non-existent
Unit test: invalidate() clears cache and next call re-parses
Verify stream-json does not block the extension host during parse (non-blocking async)
features.implementation_notes: Use stream-json with streamValues + filter to extract only the nodes section. The manifest is at target/manifest.json relative to workspace root. Models in manifest are keyed like 'model.project_name.model_name'. Column info includes name, data_type, description. This runs in the extension host (Node.js), not the webview.

features.name: Implement DomainService for reading semantic domain JSON
features.description: Create DomainService (src/services/domainService.ts) with read operations: listDomains() to discover all domain JSON files under models/semantic/, getDomain(layer, domain) to read and parse a specific domain file. Return typed SemanticDomain objects. Define TypeScript types in src/types/semantic.ts covering the full semantic domain JSON schema (schemaVersion, domain, layer, description, models, relationships, viewConfig).
validation_criteria: Unit test: listDomains discovers all .json files under models/semantic/ grouped by layer
Unit test: getDomain reads and parses a valid domain file into a typed SemanticDomain object
Unit test: getDomain handles missing files with appropriate error
Verify TypeScript types match the semantic domain JSON schema from the plan
features.implementation_notes: Files live at {dbt_project}/models/semantic/{layer}/{domain}.json. Use VS Code workspace APIs for file access. Types in src/types/semantic.ts should include: SemanticDomain, SemanticModel (with source: 'repo' | 'design'), ColumnDef, Relationship, ViewConfig. Include schemaVersion checking.

features.name: Create DomainTreeProvider for sidebar tree view
features.description: Implement DomainTreeProvider (src/providers/DomainTreeProvider.ts) as a VS Code TreeDataProvider that lists all semantic domains grouped by layer (bronze, silver, gold) in the sidebar. Show model count and design model count as badges. Include a 'New Domain...' item at the bottom. Clicking a domain should open its graph editor.
validation_criteria: Verify in Extension Development Host: sidebar shows 'Semantic Domains' view container with activity bar icon
Verify in Extension Development Host: tree view lists domains grouped under Bronze, Silver, Gold folders
Verify in Extension Development Host: each domain item shows model count badge
Verify in Extension Development Host: clicking a domain opens the graph editor panel
features.implementation_notes: Register as 'dbtSemantic.domainTree' view. Use TreeItem with collapsibleState for layer folders. Badge text format: '12 models, 3 design'. The tree view should refresh when domain files change. Layer folders appear even when empty to show available layers.

features.name: Create SemanticEditorProvider (custom text editor)
features.description: Implement SemanticEditorProvider (src/providers/SemanticEditorProvider.ts) as a CustomTextEditorProvider that opens semantic JSON files in a React webview instead of the default JSON editor. Register with viewType 'dbtSemantic.domainEditor' and selector '**/models/semantic/**/*.json' with priority 'option'. Handle the extension-webview message protocol: listen for 'ready' message from webview, send 'domainLoaded' with reconciled domain data.
validation_criteria: Verify in Extension Development Host: opening a semantic JSON file shows the custom editor (not raw JSON)
Verify in Extension Development Host: user can right-click and choose 'Open With...' to view raw JSON instead
Verify the webview receives domainLoaded message after sending 'ready'
Verify VS Code manages save/dirty state for the underlying text document
features.implementation_notes: Using CustomTextEditorProvider because semantic JSON files are text documents — VS Code manages save/dirty state. The extension host reads the document, reconciles with manifest, and sends enriched data to the webview via postMessage. Implement update loop prevention: set a pendingUpdate flag when writing via WorkspaceEdit to avoid re-sending to webview on the resulting onDidChangeTextDocument event.

features.name: Set up webview scaffold with React and React Flow
features.description: Create the webview entry point (webview/index.tsx, webview/App.tsx) with React 18 and React Flow (@xyflow/react). Set up the useVsCodeApi hook (singleton acquireVsCodeApi wrapper) and useMessageBus hook (typed message send/receive). Create the Zustand store (webview/store/editorStore.ts) for webview state. Set up VS Code CSS variable mappings in webview/styles/theme.css for theme-native styling.
validation_criteria: Verify in Extension Development Host: webview renders a React Flow canvas inside the custom editor
Verify the webview correctly acquires VS Code API and sends 'ready' message on mount
Verify theme.css maps VS Code CSS custom properties for consistent theming
Verify Zustand store initialises with default state (no selected node, detail panel closed)
features.implementation_notes: Use acquireVsCodeApi() singleton pattern — can only be called once per webview lifecycle. The webview/styles/theme.css should use VS Code's CSS custom properties (--vscode-editor-background, --vscode-editor-foreground, etc.). The Zustand store manages: mode (browse/design), selectedNode, zoom/pan, detailPanelOpen. Also integrate @vscode-elements/elements + @vscode-elements/react-elements for VS Code-native form elements.

features.name: Implement ModelNode component
features.description: Create the ModelNode React component (webview/components/Graph/ModelNode.tsx) for displaying model cards in the React Flow canvas. Show model name with layer badge (e.g. [SLV]), list columns with PK (key icon) and FK (link icon) indicators, column data types, and a column count footer. Apply green border for built models, orange for design models, and grey for missing models.
validation_criteria: Verify in Extension Development Host: model nodes display with correct name and layer badge
Verify in Extension Development Host: columns show PK/FK indicators and data types
Verify in Extension Development Host: built models have green border, design models have orange border, missing models have grey border
Verify in Extension Development Host: column count is shown in the footer
features.implementation_notes: Register as a custom React Flow node type. React Flow handles for FK edges should connect at specific column positions (for ELK port constraints). Colour values: green #22c55e, orange #f97316, grey #6b7280. Design model nodes have an orange header bar. The layer badge reads from the schema field for design models.

features.name: Implement FkEdge component
features.description: Create the FkEdge React component (webview/components/Graph/FkEdge.tsx) for displaying FK relationship edges in the React Flow canvas. Show cardinality labels on edges. Apply blue colour for built relationships and orange for design relationships. Use dashed lines for 1:1 cardinality and solid lines for many-to-one / one-to-many.
validation_criteria: Verify in Extension Development Host: FK edges render between connected models
Verify in Extension Development Host: edge labels show cardinality (e.g. 'many-to-one')
Verify in Extension Development Host: built relationships are blue (#3b82f6), design relationships are orange (#f97316)
Verify in Extension Development Host: 1:1 edges are dashed, many-to-one edges are solid
features.implementation_notes: Register as a custom React Flow edge type. Edge colours: blue #3b82f6 (built), orange #f97316 (design). Relationship identity is composite key: (fromModel, fromColumn, toModel, toColumn), supporting multiple FKs between the same models.

features.name: Implement graph transformer (models to React Flow nodes/edges)
features.description: Create graphTransformer (webview/lib/graphTransformer.ts) that converts a ReconciledDomain (pre-resolved by ReconciliationService) into React Flow nodes and edges. The transformer is now simplified — it just maps the shape since columns and status are already resolved. Map each ReconciledModel to a ModelFlowNode with position from viewConfig.positions, and each ReconciledRelationship to an FkFlowEdge.
validation_criteria: Unit test: transformer converts a domain with 3 models and 2 relationships into correct React Flow nodes and edges
Unit test: positions are loaded from viewConfig.positions; models without positions default to (0,0)
Unit test: columns are passed through with status (built/planned/missing) for row styling
Verify in Extension Development Host: opening a domain renders all models and edges correctly positioned
features.implementation_notes: The transformer receives ReconciledDomain from the extension host (columns and status already resolved by ReconciliationService). It maps to React Flow shapes without additional logic. The colorScheme.ts module is no longer used — status is pre-resolved. Models without a saved position default to (0, 0).

features.name: Integrate ELK layout with Auto Layout button
features.description: Implement ELK layout integration (webview/lib/elkLayout.ts) using elkjs. Set up the ELK Web Worker using blob URL pattern (VS Code webviews cannot use importScripts). Create the Auto Layout button in the toolbar that runs ELK over the full graph and writes resulting positions back to viewConfig.positions. Show a confirmation dialog if positions already exist ('This will rearrange all nodes. Continue?'). Default ELK options: layered algorithm, RIGHT direction, ORTHOGONAL edge routing, 16:9 aspect ratio, FIXED_ORDER port constraints.
validation_criteria: Verify in Extension Development Host: clicking 'Auto Layout' arranges all nodes in a clean layered layout
Verify in Extension Development Host: confirmation dialog appears when positions already exist
Verify ELK runs in a Web Worker and does not block the UI thread
Verify new positions are persisted to the domain JSON viewConfig.positions
features.implementation_notes: VS Code webviews cannot use importScripts or dynamic import() for workers. Bundle the ELK worker into a single file with esbuild, then load via blob URL: import elkWorkerCode from './elk-worker.js?raw'; const workerBlob = new Blob([elkWorkerCode], { type: 'text/javascript' }); const workerUrl = URL.createObjectURL(workerBlob); const elk = new ELK({ workerUrl }). Default ELK config is stored in domain JSON viewConfig.layoutOptions and can be overridden per-domain.

features.name: Implement node position persistence
features.description: Enable drag-to-reposition of model nodes with debounced persistence. When a user drags a node, update that model's entry in viewConfig.positions immediately in the webview state, then debounce the write to the semantic domain JSON file via the extension host. Positions are loaded from viewConfig.positions on open. Auto Layout overwrites all positions.
validation_criteria: Verify in Extension Development Host: dragging a node saves its new position to the domain JSON
Verify debouncing: rapid drags result in a single write, not one per pixel
Verify positions persist across editor close and reopen
Verify Auto Layout button overwrites all manual positions
features.implementation_notes: Positions live in viewConfig.positions in the domain JSON, committed to git so all users see the same layout. Send updatePositions message to extension host with debounced positions. The extension host writes via WorkspaceEdit. On open, positions are loaded from the JSON; models without positions get (0,0).

features.name: Implement ReconciliationService with overlay semantics
features.description: Create ReconciliationService (src/services/reconciliationService.ts) that merges semantic domain JSON with manifest data using 'overlay semantics'. For repo models: manifest columns (green) + plannedColumns not in manifest (orange). For design models: inline columns (all orange). PK designated via 'primaryKey' field on repo models. FK inferred from relationships array. Columns shown with status-based row colouring: green for built, orange for planned/missing.
validation_criteria: Unit test: design model not in manifest → status ORANGE, columns from inline definition
Unit test: design model found in manifest → status GREEN, columns from manifest
Unit test: repo model found in manifest → status GREEN, columns from manifest + plannedColumns not in manifest (orange)
Unit test: repo model not in manifest → status GREY (missing)
Unit test: plannedColumn that exists in manifest is skipped (manifest wins)
Unit test: PK/FK references to non-existent columns show as orange ghost rows
Visual test: green column rows for built columns, orange for planned, separator between them
features.implementation_notes: Column resolution uses overlay semantics: (1) Start with manifest columns (green/built), (2) Add plannedColumns not in manifest (orange/planned), (3) Add ghost rows for PK/FK references to non-existent columns (orange/missing). The SemanticModel type now includes 'primaryKey' (string) for repo models and 'plannedColumns' (ColumnDef[]) for forward-planning. ReconciliationService is called in SemanticEditorProvider.sendDomainData() before sending to webview. ModelNode displays columns with status-based row styling and a 'PLANNED' separator.

features.name: Create toolbar with zoom, fit view, and mode display
features.description: Implement the Toolbar component (webview/components/Toolbar/Toolbar.tsx) with zoom in/out buttons, fit view button (centres the graph), Auto Layout button (triggers ELK), and domain info display (domain name and layer). Include a status bar at the bottom showing model count and relationship count. Phase 2 will add '+ Model' and '+ Relationship' buttons.
validation_criteria: Verify in Extension Development Host: toolbar renders at the top of the graph editor
Verify in Extension Development Host: zoom and fit view buttons work correctly
Verify in Extension Development Host: domain name and layer are displayed in the toolbar
Verify in Extension Development Host: status bar at the bottom shows model and relationship counts
features.implementation_notes: The toolbar is the top bar of the graph editor. Use React Flow's built-in zoom/pan controls API. Status bar format: '12 models (3 design) | 18 relationships'. Auto Layout button is wired to the ELK layout feature (F109).

features.name: Implement detail panel for model inspection
features.description: Create the ModelDetail component (webview/components/DetailPanel/ModelDetail.tsx) that shows detailed information about the selected model node in a side panel. Display: model name, layer/schema, source (repo/design), status (built/design/missing), full column list with data types and PK/FK indicators, and FK relationships involving this model. The panel opens when a node is clicked and can be collapsed.
validation_criteria: Verify in Extension Development Host: clicking a model node opens the detail panel on the right
Verify in Extension Development Host: detail panel shows model name, status, and all columns
Verify in Extension Development Host: PK and FK columns are indicated
Verify in Extension Development Host: panel can be collapsed and reopened
features.implementation_notes: The detail panel sits on the right side of the graph editor layout. For Phase 1, it's read-only. Column editing comes in Phase 2 (F203). Use @vscode-elements for table-like display of columns.

features.name: Implement webview state restoration
features.description: Implement state persistence using VS Code's getState()/setState() API so UI state survives when the webview is hidden and revealed. Persist: zoom level, pan offset, selected node name, detail panel open/closed state. On reveal, the webview sends 'ready' message, receives fresh domain data from extension host, then applies persisted UI state on top.
validation_criteria: Verify in Extension Development Host: switch to another tab, switch back — zoom and pan position are restored
Verify in Extension Development Host: selected node and detail panel state are restored after tab switch
Verify domain data is re-fetched fresh on restore (not stale cached data)
Verify this does not use retainContextWhenHidden
features.implementation_notes: This avoids retainContextWhenHidden which keeps the webview in memory permanently and increases resource usage. Persisted state (getState/setState): zoom, pan, selectedNode, mode, detailPanelOpen. Fresh data: full domain + reconciled status + positions. On reveal: webview sends 'ready', receives domainLoaded, applies persisted UI state.

features.name: Define shared TypeScript types and message protocol
features.description: Create comprehensive TypeScript type definitions for the extension-webview communication. In src/types/semantic.ts: SemanticDomain, SemanticModel, ColumnDef, Relationship, ViewConfig, DomainSummary, DesignModel, ReconciledDomain, ReconciledModel. In src/types/messages.ts: ExtensionMessage union type (domainLoaded, domainUpdated, manifestRefreshed, error) and WebviewMessage union type (ready, addModel, addColumn, removeColumn, addRelationship, removeModel, removeRelationship, updateViewConfig, addExistingModel, updatePositions, runAutoLayout).
validation_criteria: Types compile without errors under both tsconfig.json and tsconfig.webview.json
All message types are exhaustively handled in both extension host and webview message handlers
SemanticDomain type matches the JSON schema defined in the plan
Types are importable from both extension host and webview code
features.implementation_notes: These types are shared between extension host and webview. Ensure they are compatible with both Node.js and DOM TypeScript configs. The message protocol is categorised by direction: Extension→Webview and Webview→Extension as defined in the plan.

features.name: Wire up extension activation and command registration
features.description: Implement extension.ts with activate() and deactivate() functions. In activate: initialise ManifestService, DomainService, ReconciliationService, register the DomainTreeProvider, register the SemanticEditorProvider, register all commands (createDomain, openDomain, deleteDomain, refreshManifest). Detect the dbt project root from workspace. The extension activates on workspaceContains:**/dbt_project.yml.
validation_criteria: Verify in Extension Development Host: extension activates when opening a folder containing dbt_project.yml
Verify in Extension Development Host: all commands appear in the command palette under 'dbt' category
Verify in Extension Development Host: sidebar tree view loads with domain listing
Verify in Extension Development Host: opening a semantic JSON file shows the custom editor
features.implementation_notes: Lazy-load services to avoid slowing VS Code activation. The extension detects the project root by finding dbt_project.yml in the workspace. All services are initialised with this project path. Use VS Code Disposable pattern for cleanup in deactivate().

features.name: Add Model button in toolbar
features.description: Add a permanent '+ Model' button to the toolbar (always visible, no mode toggle needed). Clicking opens the New Model dialog. This replaces the previous browse/design mode toggle approach — the visual distinction between built (green) and planned (orange) items IS the mode indicator. Selection enables editing in the detail panel.
validation_criteria: Verify in Extension Development Host: toolbar shows '+ Model' button at all times
Verify in Extension Development Host: clicking '+ Model' opens the new model dialog
Verify in Extension Development Host: the button uses VS Code-native styling
features.implementation_notes: Single-mode approach: no browse/design toggle. The color scheme (green=built, orange=planned) communicates state. Selection enables editing in the detail panel. Remove the EditorMode type from the store — it's no longer needed.

features.name: Implement New Model dialog with JHG templates
features.description: Create NewModelDialog component (webview/components/Dialogs/NewModelDialog.tsx) for creating design models. Fields: model name, schema, layer (auto-set from domain), description, and template picker. Templates: Dimension (dim_), Fact (fct_), Bridge (brg_), SCD Type 2, Blank. Templates pre-populate columns according to JHG conventions. Placeholder resolution: {name} derived from model name minus prefix, {left}/{right} fields for bridge template. On submit, send addModel message to extension host.
validation_criteria: Verify in Extension Development Host: clicking '+ Model' opens the new model dialog
Verify in Extension Development Host: selecting 'Dimension' template pre-populates standard dim columns with {name}_id PK
Verify in Extension Development Host: Bridge template shows Left/Right entity fields
Verify in Extension Development Host: submitting the dialog creates an orange design model node on the canvas
Verify the design model is persisted to the semantic domain JSON file
features.implementation_notes: Templates: Dimension (dim_) has {name}_id PK, name, description, is_active, valid_from, valid_to, dwh_inserted_at, dwh_updated_at. Fact (fct_) has {name}_id PK, event_date, amount, dwh_inserted_at, dwh_updated_at. Bridge (brg_) has {name}_id PK, {left}_id FK, {right}_id FK, dwh_inserted_at. SCD2 extends dim with scd_valid_from, scd_valid_to, scd_is_current, scd_hash. Blank has no columns. If model name doesn't start with expected prefix, {name} falls back to full model name. Templates are configurable via extension settings.

features.name: Implement unified column editor in detail panel
features.description: Extend the DetailPanel to support column editing when a model is selected. The behavior depends on model/column status: (1) Built models show read-only built columns (green) plus an 'Add Planned Column' button to add orange columns that will be built later. (2) Planned models (source: design) show all columns as editable. (3) Planned columns on any model can be edited or deleted. (4) Built columns are always read-only. New Column Dialog fields: column name, data type dropdown, description, is primary key checkbox.
validation_criteria: Verify in Extension Development Host: selecting any model opens the detail panel with column list
Verify in Extension Development Host: built columns (green) are read-only with no edit/delete controls
Verify in Extension Development Host: planned columns (orange) show edit and delete buttons
Verify in Extension Development Host: 'Add Planned Column' button appears for both built and planned models
Verify in Extension Development Host: column changes persist to the semantic domain JSON
features.implementation_notes: No mode toggle needed — selection is the trigger. Built models use 'plannedColumns' array for new columns. Design models use inline 'columns' array. The visual separator between built and planned columns already exists from F111. Use @vscode-elements for form controls.

features.name: Implement New Relationship dialog
features.description: Create NewFkDialog component (webview/components/Dialogs/NewFkDialog.tsx) for creating FK relationships between models. Add a '+ Relationship' button to the toolbar (next to + Model). Flow: select source model → source column → target model → target column → cardinality (many-to-one / one-to-one). On submit, send addRelationship message to extension host. The relationship is marked with source: 'design' and renders as an orange edge.
validation_criteria: Verify in Extension Development Host: toolbar shows '+ Relationship' button
Verify in Extension Development Host: clicking it opens the FK dialog
Verify in Extension Development Host: dialog allows selecting source model, column, target model, column, and cardinality
Verify in Extension Development Host: submitting creates an orange FK edge on the canvas
Verify the relationship is persisted to the semantic domain JSON with source: 'design'
features.implementation_notes: Cardinality options: many-to-one, one-to-one. Relationship identity is composite key: (fromModel, fromColumn, toModel, toColumn). This supports multiple FK edges between the same pair of models. Use @vscode-elements dropdowns populated with available models and their columns.

features.name: Implement drag-to-connect FK creation
features.description: Enable creating FK relationships by dragging from a column handle on one model node to another model node on the canvas. When the drag completes, open a simplified relationship dialog pre-filled with the source model and target model, allowing the user to select specific columns and cardinality. This is an alternative to the full New Relationship dialog. Always enabled (no mode gate).
validation_criteria: Verify in Extension Development Host: dragging from a model handle to another model initiates FK creation
Verify in Extension Development Host: the connection dialog pre-fills source and target models
Verify in Extension Development Host: completing the flow creates an orange FK edge
Verify in Extension Development Host: drag-to-connect works at all times (no mode restriction)
features.implementation_notes: Use React Flow's onConnect callback and custom connection line. The drag starts from a handle on the source model node. On connect, open the NewFkDialog pre-filled with source and target models. No mode check needed.

features.name: Implement delete actions for planned items
features.description: Enable deleting planned models, planned columns, and design relationships. Delete button in detail panel (disabled/hidden for built items). Support Delete key when a planned item is selected. Deleting a design model also removes all its relationships. Show confirmation dialog before deleting models. Built models and built columns cannot be deleted — the delete button is disabled or hidden for these.
validation_criteria: Verify in Extension Development Host: selecting a planned model shows enabled Delete button in detail panel
Verify in Extension Development Host: selecting a built model shows disabled/hidden Delete button
Verify in Extension Development Host: planned columns show delete icon, built columns do not
Verify in Extension Development Host: deleting a model also removes its FK edges
Verify in Extension Development Host: confirmation dialog appears before model deletion
Verify deletions persist to the semantic domain JSON
features.implementation_notes: Send removeModel, removeColumn, removeRelationship messages to extension host. The extension host updates the JSON and sends back domainUpdated. Cascade delete: removing a model also removes all relationships where it is fromModel or toModel. Delete is only enabled for status: 'design' models and status: 'planned' columns.

features.name: Implement DomainService write operations
features.description: Extend DomainService with full write operations: addDesignModel, addRelationship, removeModel, removeRelationship, addColumn (to plannedColumns for repo models, to columns for design models), removeColumn. All writes use VS Code's WorkspaceEdit API to modify the semantic domain JSON file on disk. This is the backend for all mutations.
validation_criteria: Unit test: addDesignModel adds a model with source 'design' to the domain JSON
Unit test: addColumn to repo model adds to plannedColumns array
Unit test: addColumn to design model adds to columns array
Unit test: addRelationship adds a relationship to the domain JSON
Unit test: removeModel removes the model and cascading relationships
Unit test: all write operations produce valid JSON matching the schema
Verify writes use WorkspaceEdit so VS Code tracks dirty state and undo history
features.implementation_notes: IMPLEMENTED IN SemanticEditorProvider: All write operations (handleAddModel, handleAddColumn, handleUpdateColumn, handleRemoveColumn, handleAddRelationship, handleRemoveModel, handleRemoveRelationship) were implemented directly in SemanticEditorProvider.ts (lines 194-805) rather than in DomainService. This architectural choice keeps DomainService as a pure read service while the editor provider handles all mutations via WorkspaceEdit, providing tight VS Code integration (undo/redo, dirty state). The pendingUpdate flag prevents update loops from onDidChangeTextDocument events.

features.name: Implement undo/redo via WorkspaceEdit
features.description: Ensure all mutations (add/remove model, column, relationship) work with VS Code's built-in undo/redo. Since all writes go through WorkspaceEdit, VS Code's Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z should undo/redo changes. Verify the webview re-renders correctly after undo/redo by handling onDidChangeTextDocument events.
validation_criteria: Verify in Extension Development Host: Ctrl+Z undoes the last change
Verify in Extension Development Host: Ctrl+Shift+Z redoes an undone change
Verify the graph canvas updates correctly after undo/redo
Verify multi-step undo works (add model → add column → undo → undo restores original state)
features.implementation_notes: WorkspaceEdit-based writes automatically integrate with VS Code's undo stack. The extension host listens for onDidChangeTextDocument — on external changes (including undo), re-read the JSON, reconcile, and send domainUpdated to the webview. The update loop prevention flag ensures self-originated writes don't trigger redundant updates.

features.name: Implement validation for operations
features.description: Add validation rules for all operations: prevent duplicate model names within a domain, prevent duplicate column names within a model, prevent circular FK references, ensure FK target columns exist, prevent creating a relationship where the composite key (fromModel, fromColumn, toModel, toColumn) already exists. Show validation errors using VS Code-native error elements.
validation_criteria: Verify in Extension Development Host: attempting to create a model with an existing name shows an error
Verify in Extension Development Host: attempting to create a duplicate column shows an error
Verify in Extension Development Host: attempting to create a duplicate FK (same composite key) shows an error
Verify in Extension Development Host: validation errors display inline in the dialog
features.implementation_notes: Validation runs client-side in the webview before sending messages to the extension host. Use @vscode-elements for error display. Circular FK detection: check if adding a new FK would create a cycle in the relationship graph (A→B→C→A).

features.name: Implement Create Domain command
features.description: Create the 'Create Semantic Domain' command (src/commands/createDomain.ts) that opens a dialog for creating a new domain. Fields: domain name (slug), layer (bronze/silver/gold dropdown), description. Creates the JSON file at models/semantic/{layer}/{domain}.json with the initial schema (schemaVersion: 1, empty models/relationships, default viewConfig). Updates the tree view to show the new domain.

features.name: Anti-pattern validation using modelling metadata
features.description: Implement validation rules that use the structured modelling metadata (modelRole, grain, scdType, additiveType) to detect common data modelling anti-patterns from the modelling workflow. Validations run on domain load and after edits, producing warnings (not errors) displayed as a collapsible section in the DetailPanel and as warning badges on affected nodes. Rules: (1) Missing grain — models without a grain statement get a warning. (2) Dimension attributes in facts — columns without isForeignKey on a fact-role model that have STRING/VARCHAR type and no additiveType set, suggesting they may be descriptive attributes that belong in a dimension. (3) Measures in dimensions — columns with additiveType set on a dimension-role model. (4) Pre-computed ratios — columns on fact models with names matching *_pct, *_ratio, *_rate, *_percent suggesting pre-computed ratios that should be stored as numerator/denominator components. (5) Missing SCD strategy — dimension columns without scdType when the model has role set. (6) Conformed dim duplication — a model with role 'domain-dim' whose name matches a known conformed dimension pattern. Warnings are dismissible per-model (stored in viewConfig so they persist but don't block workflow). Each warning links to the relevant section of the modelling workflow documentation.

features.implementation_notes: Create a new ValidationService (src/services/validationService.ts) that takes a ReconciledDomain and returns warnings per model. Warning interface: `{ modelName: string; rule: string; message: string; severity: 'warning'; column?: string }`. Run validation in ReconciliationService after reconciliation — attach warnings to ReconciledModel as `warnings?: ValidationWarning[]`. The webview renders warnings in DetailPanel as a collapsible 'Modelling Warnings' section with yellow/amber styling (matching the existing discrepancy warning pattern). Node badge: reuse the discrepancy badge pattern but with a different icon/colour for modelling warnings vs structural discrepancies. Dismissals stored in viewConfig.dismissedWarnings as `Record<string, string[]>` (model name → array of dismissed rule IDs). Validation only runs on models that have modelRole set — models without role are unvalidated (supports gradual adoption). Keep rules simple and high-confidence to avoid alert fatigue — it's better to have 5 useful warnings than 20 noisy ones.
